stem: A 6-year-old has a recurrent swelling on the inner lower lip after habitual lip-biting; which diagnosis best fits?
explanation: Mucocoele is the best fit. This is because minor salivary glands are present in the lower lip, and lip-biting can cause a mucocoele with recurrent swelling at that site.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because mucocoeles commonly arise from minor salivary gland trauma, especially after lip-biting, and present as a recurrent lower-lip swelling.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because mumps typically causes parotid gland swelling, not a local recurrent swelling on the inner lower lip.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because aphthous ulcers are painful mucosal ulcers rather than a recurrent cyst-like swelling after lip-biting.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because herpetic gingivostomatitis causes gingival and oral vesicular lesions, not an isolated recurrent lower-lip swelling.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because facial cellulitis of dental origin causes diffuse facial soft tissue infection rather than a localised lower-lip lesion.
